public_final_quotes: Reviewed the full current prefix C:T000–C:T013 and all legal past sessions H001–H012. The current-turn evidence consistently attributes the helpful chat and perspective to an old college friend, not to this AI. No legal evidence shows a prior conversation between the user and this AI about the thesis. R002 contains no independent personal factual claim.

R001 materially misattributes the user’s prior helpful conversation to the current AI: the seeker explicitly identified an old college friend as the person who messaged them and helped them gain perspective. The follow-up question is reflective, but it is built on that incorrect self-attribution, so a dominant boundary/factual error undermines the support.

C:T005 identifies the support as coming from an old college friend; C:T009 describes what that friend said; C:T013 says the chat with that friend helped the user see things differently. No supplied evidence shows that the current AI had that conversation. 'Talking with me' turns the friend’s completed helpful action into the current AI’s action, a material role/identity error.

This is a reflective question asking what part of the perspective is worth holding onto, not an assertion of a new personal fact. It is nevertheless weakened by the preceding misattribution, which is assessed separately in R001.
